title: ES v1 tests take too long
body: ``` $ go test -race ./internal/storage/v1/elasticsearch/ ok github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/internal/storage/v1/elasticsearch 11.506s ``` Running with profiler ``` $ GOMAXPROCS=1 go test -parallel 128 -p 16 -json ./internal/storage/v1/elasticsearch/ | go run github.com/roblaszczak/vgt@latest ``` shows 3 tests blocking for 5 seconds each

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
for https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/bafa50774a2b4d687642fa26875f1308a15c9cb8/internal/storage/v1/elasticsearch/factory_test.go#L277C1-L364C1  we can Reduce the timeout values in the `assert.Eventually` calls . Since these are unit tests using an in-memory HTTP test server, they should complete much faster .


https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/bafa50774a2b4d687642fa26875f1308a15c9cb8/internal/storage/v1/elasticsearch/factory_test.go#L250C1-L259C2 and https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/bafa50774a2b4d687642fa26875f1308a15c9cb8/internal/storage/v1/elasticsearch/factoryv1_test.go#L104C1-L127C2 tests are  taking approx 5 seconds each primarily due to timeouts occurring when these tests attempted to connect to a non-existent Elasticsearch  server in test cases . The Elasticsearch client library has a default health check timeout of 5 seconds that is causing the extra time . instead of checking the real network calls for es server we can  mock the error to eliminate the timeout , is it correct ?? @reporter

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: the test is meant to test error handling when not able to connect to the db server. It may be possible to mock something underneath the HTTP client (like roundtripper) to return an error immediately.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: Hey @reporter i was working on this one and trying out different approaches. The results that i got with different configurations are as :- 1. If we just run the blocking tests in parallel then we get the time down to 5 seconds. 2. I tried mocking the network response using `httptest` but it resulted in no gain and only other way the tests improved were if the client was initialized to error out using `FactoryBase` like ``` f := &FactoryBase{ config: &cfg, } f.newClientFn = func(_ context.Context, _ *escfg.Configuration, _ *zap.Logger, _ metrics.Factory) (es.Client, error) { return nil, errors.New("failed to create Elasticsearch client") ``` But these might not be testing the connecting mechanism of ES client correctly. Can you please suggest something else that i could try. Thanks.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> If we just run the blocking tests in parallel then we get the time down to 5 seconds.

that's already a good speedup over the current sequential execution.

But the main question is - what's taking 5 seconds? starting a server with connection should be faster than that.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: @reporter i did debugging and profiling and found that the `healthCheck` was causing problems and the 5 second timeout even before connecting to the server. upon disabling it in the configuration tests are faster. but sometimes it making a `goleak` error like but if i set the connection url like `localhost:65535` instead of `http://127.0.0.1:65535` then the error is not there and tests run fine. Also i was not able to disable the `healthCheck` in case of the below test which still slows down the overall test to 5 seconds. ``` { name: "server error", factory: NewFactory(), expectedErr: "failed to create Elasticsearch client: health check timeout: Head \"http://127.0.0.1:9200\": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:9200: connect: connection refused: no Elasticsearch node available", } ``` Can you suggest if anything else that i can also try for these cases. Thanks.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Also i was not able to disable the healthCheck in case of the below test which still slows down the overall test to 5 seconds.

Do we have control over healthCheck timeout here? We want to set it very small. Even better if we can mock the http client to return error immediately, because the test is just testing error handling in the factory. Or perhaps we could pass an invalid host name instead, e.g. `http://invalid-host-name:9200` which might fail even sooner (but might also fail in the wrong place and affect code coverage, to need to test).

please create a PR for the speedup you already have

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: > Do we have control over healthCheck timeout here? We want to set it very small. Yes @reporter we can set the timeout. i tried this and upon setting the timeout to 1 second the tests finish in 1 second indeed. In the PR should i just manually set the timeout to 1 second or make this also configurable like the `disableHealthCheck` parameter ? as i believe 1 second might be too less in real world.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Disabling health checks if they are not relevant to a specific test is even better. The danger with small time outs is they could lead to flaky tests that do time out in the busy CI runner.
